_comment: Reference token counts for cl100k_base, the encoding used by GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.
Every entry is restricted to a construction whose cl100k_base segmentation is
unambiguous and can be derived from the encoding's published pre-tokenizer rules
- a common English word, optionally preceded by a single space, is one token;
- a run of digits is split left to right into groups of at most three, and a
single leading space joins the first group;
- an ASCII punctuation character is one token;
- a whitespace run that is not absorbed by a following word is one token.
Strings whose segmentation depends on the merge table in ways that cannot be
derived by hand -- URLs, code, rare words, non-Latin scripts -- are deliberately
absent. Their absence is the honest limit of this corpus: the measured error
below applies to English prose and numeric text, not to source code.
To extend the corpus with a real encoder, add entries and replace the derived
counts with encoder output; the test does not care where the numbers came from.
